steps.title: ce, cet, cette, ces
steps.body: Use a demonstrative before a noun when you point to something or identify which thing you mean. In English, these forms can mean this, that, these or those; the situation shows whether the item is near or farther away.

steps.title: This / that / these / those
rows: masculine singular noun starting with a consonant
masculine singular noun starting with a vowel or silent h

steps.title: ce, cet, cette, ces
steps.body:
• Choose the form from the noun, not the English word this or that.
• Use cet only with a masculine singular noun that begins with a vowel sound: cet article.
• ce + noun is different from c'est: Ce pantalon est bleu (this/that pair of pants); C'est un pantalon bleu (It is blue pants).

steps.title: Watch out
steps.body: Cet and cette sound alike in standard French. Listen for the noun and its gender: cet article is masculine; cette étiquette is feminine.

steps.explain: Panier is masculine singular and starts with a consonant: ce panier.
Article is masculine singular and starts with a vowel: cet article.
Chemise is feminine singular: cette chemise.

steps.prompt: Which sentence means “this shirt is on sale”?
steps.explain: Chemise is feminine singular, so use cette.
